leak-scan.reason: ON, no exceptions (design §3.3). This repo's payload is `.md` and `.py` — templates extracted FROM private repos — so the corpus-only scope that fits claude-code-cache-fix is blind here: a foreign home path in a template is exactly the leak direction this repo exists on the wrong side of, and no fixture corpus would ever see it. The scanner-side half of this key is a residue, recorded in ITEMS.md: the shipped `foreign-path` class is scoped `corpus`, so honouring this declaration means widening it to source scope, and the scanner is a byte-identical copy that lands in claude-code-cache-fix first.

investigation records.staleness: change-coupling — a record whose NOW no longer composes its ESTABLISHED lines toward GOAL is stale by the format's own slot discipline and is rewritten before the next probe is chosen. The ESTABLISHED lines themselves age like any cited basis: a line whose command, file or output has moved past the citation no longer establishes what it claims.

exit.recording-act: a `## CLOSED` heading whose body carries the graduation pointers — ESTABLISHED lines to the ledger or docs of the repo they describe, OPEN lines to the item carrier or a recorded one-line disposition. `lifecycle record check` refuses a closure that is undrained or unpointed.
exit.detail: THE FILE NEVER MOVES INTO ANY TREE, and that is the stage rather than an omission. Closure here is GRADUATION of the record's CONTENT, never relocation of the file: the body goes to the carrier that will be re-read, and the record stays in XDG state as history. The three benefits the format file names are what the home protects — no repo is dirtied, no permission dialog fires from the `.claude`-shape protection, and the record survives across repo states and branches, which is exactly what a multi-session arc needs. `the fire log` is the precedent: a machine-wide XDG path declared as a per-repo kind with all six stages.

investigation records.growth: unbounded-with-reason — one file per project+arc, and an arc opens only when work turns diagnosis-shaped or passes a skip-gauge no. The flow control is the closure gate rather than a count: a record cannot close with undrained slots, so an arc that ends leaves its lines in the carriers that consume them instead of accumulating here. A cap would bound the LABEL and be escaped by opening a second arc (R22).
investigation records.trigger: none, declared why: a record opens when work turns diagnosis-shaped — the next call exists to explain the previous call's output — and that reading is the session's own

exit.detail: WAVE 3 — delete oldest past three. That is an EXIT RULE and not a cap: what leaves is the oldest by parsed semver, red-proven on the real listing where `0.9` string-sorts above `0.11` The drift DETECTOR that reads this kind is wave 3's and is not named as a reader here: a `producer:` reference resolves against the producers this declaration's kinds actually name, and naming one the machine has no home for is law 23's own case — a thing named without its home.

design notes.staleness: change-coupling — a design note is stale once the item it carries closes, or once a framing it states is superseded by evidence. MEASURED INSTANCE, which is why this stage reads this way: answerable-not-felt.md states momentum-independence as the desk/peer mechanism, and three research lanes refuted it in favour of INDEPENDENCE (arXiv:2603.26993) — the note's own text was stale the day after it was written, while resolving and reading as current.

exit.recording-act: at its item's closure the note's ESTABLISHED claims graduate to the laws file or the ledger and the note moves to docs/directives/ as the arc's persisted design record; the closing ledger line names the commit. Closure by graduation, never deletion.
exit.detail: NOT MOVED WHILE LIVE, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: on 2026-09-18 four citations of `docs/answerable-not-felt.md` stood in THREE artifacts outside this repo's write boundary — a peer's arc investigation record under XDG state, a dotfiles directive, and a CachyOS-Setup directive — every one by repo-relative path. Relocating a live note breaks each of them silently, which is the citation-rot class lc-155 exists to catch. So the home claims the note where it already sits, and the move waits for the closure that re-roots its citations.

design notes.growth: bounded-by-exit — one note per design arc, and each leaves by the graduation above when its item closes. The flow control is that a note cannot be born without an item to carry it.
design notes.trigger: none, declared why: a design note is written when a design is settled, which is the end of a judgment and not a state

begehung findings.staleness: change-coupling — a findings file whose cited artifact lines have moved past the citation no longer measures anything current. Its ROUND is closed once and never re-opened, so the file is historical from its close; what ages is the artifact it cites, not the reading.

exit.recording-act: none is taken: append-only historical, one file per closed round. A later round that re-walks the same axis cites the earlier file rather than superseding it — the MAP's axis row carries the current yield, the findings file carries how it was reached.
exit.detail: REGISTERED BECAUSE THE SWEEP CAUGHT IT, 2026-09-18: the file was tracked and resolved to no kind, so `kind sweep` exited 2 and the declared verify block was red for every writer in the repo until this landed. Worth keeping as the reason: a robustness review's own OUTPUT is exactly the kind of persisted thing this plugin exists to give a home, and the review tripped the invariant it was reviewing for. The alternatives were lc-76's declared-custom disposition (wrong shape — that is for a one-off file, this is a recurring class, one per round) and leaving it untracked (which loses the round's deliverable; the skill names the findings file as exactly that).

begehung findings.growth: unbounded-with-reason — one file per closed round, and a round happens only when a walk is run. The flow control is that a round cannot close without its findings file, and cannot open while another is open.
begehung findings.trigger: none, declared why: a round is walked when someone decides to walk one; the decision is the event

desk state.staleness: none, declared why: the verb ALWAYS OVERWRITES and keeps no history, so a desk's state is current by construction — there is no older value for a newer one to be stale against. What CAN go stale is a file whose desk no longer exists, and that is residue for the exit rather than staleness of a live fact.

exit.recording-act: a ledger decision line naming the desk ids whose state was removed and why each was judged gone
exit.detail: DECLARED, NOT IMPLEMENTED (law 15 permits the state and law 22 forbids pretending otherwise): no verb removes a dead desk's state today. It is not a compaction — there is nothing to fold, since each file holds one desk's current state and no history — and it is not `never`, because a desk that no longer exists leaves a file nothing will ever read again.

desk state.growth: unbounded-with-reason — one file per DESK ID, overwritten in place, so the count tracks desks that have ever stored state and never activity: a desk writing a thousand times leaves one file. The flow this kind would be controlled by is therefore the desk population, which is not a rate this plugin produces. Declared unbounded rather than `bounded-by-exit` because the latter would assert a control the delete exit does not yet perform — the assurance wider than its predicate, in the stage that describes the control.
